# SSLense

> SSLense is a free, open-source (Apache-2.0) Windows application that obtains Let’s Encrypt SSL certificates for IIS websites, binds them, verifies them over HTTPS and renews them automatically. It also installs and monitors certificates bought from other providers, and sends a daily expiry reminder digest. It has a desktop GUI, a command line and a background renewal service.

## Key pages
- [Home](https://sslense.com/): what SSLense does, features, command-line examples and FAQ
- [How to install a free SSL certificate on IIS with Let’s Encrypt](https://sslense.com/guides/install-ssl-iis-lets-encrypt/): step-by-step guide, HTTP to HTTPS redirect, renewal checks and common errors
- [Source code](https://github.com/panchalvimaldev/sslense): repository, documentation and issue tracker
- [Releases](https://github.com/panchalvimaldev/sslense/releases): MSI installers with SHA-256 checksums

## Facts
- Platform: Windows Server with IIS
- Certificates: free domain-validated certificates from Let’s Encrypt, using HTTP-01 or DNS-01 validation, including wildcard certificates
- DNS validation: automatic renewal through Cloudflare, or through a CNAME from any DNS service to a domain on Cloudflare; a manual method for any DNS service, renewed by hand; one wildcard per IIS site for now
- Interfaces: desktop GUI, CLI (SSLense.Cli), and a Windows service that checks hourly
- Renewal: follows ACME Renewal Information (ARI), with a lifetime-relative fallback
- Notifications: email through any SMTP server or relay, Microsoft Teams, Slack, Discord, Telegram, ntfy, a heartbeat ping, and the Windows Event Log
- Certificates from other providers (such as 123-reg, Sectigo, DigiCert): certificate requests with a non-exportable key, installing the issued certificate with HTTPS verification and rollback, PFX import, and adopting certificates already bound in IIS; SSLense reminds you to order their renewals
- Reminders: one daily digest, only when a certificate needs attention, from a configurable number of days before expiry (default 30) until it is renewed; snooze or turn off per certificate; optional weekly summary; an option to keep reminding about automatic certificates until they renew; shows when the next email is due and logs why each certificate was included or skipped
- Daily checks: report-only pre-flight checks in the 30 days before each automatic renewal, and a comparison of the certificate served on port 443 from the server with the one SSLense expects; problems are reported after two failures in a row
- License: Apache License 2.0
- Status: pre-release (0.12.x); releases are not yet code-signed
- Support: GitHub issues; security reports through GitHub private vulnerability reporting
